children: Intesa Sanpaolo’s bid for €36 bln MPS could give it a leading share of Italian lending and a grip on insurance rival, Generali. Both could mean extra antitrust remedies. CEO Carlo Messina can probably manage the risks, but the range of outcomes adds to an already complex deal.
Full view will be published shortly.

Italian antitrust authorities on September 15 opened a probe into Intesa Sanpaolo's bid for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena. The offer may raise competition issues in 20 provinces regarding deposits and 17 regarding small business lending, competition regulators said.
